activity.title: Blow the Paper Ball
activity.goal: Practise long, slow breaths out through play.
activity.safety: One whole sheet crumpled into one big ball: no small torn pieces, and nothing in the mouth. A few slow breaths, then a rest. Stop if the child feels dizzy. Wash hands afterwards (newspaper ink). If there is an accident, call your local emergency number.
activity.forAdult: In the story, Grandma helps Yara calm down by breathing slowly with her: in… out… This game practises the same long, slow breath out, through play. Grown-ups use slow breaths to calm down, and a rolling ball turns a breath into something a toddler can see. Crumple a whole sheet of newspaper into one big ball together. The child can help squeeze it. Lie on your tummies, face to face, about an arm’s length apart. Breathe in, then blow out slowly and for a long time, “whoooo”, so the ball rolls to the child. Then the child blows it back. Praise the long, slow breath, not the speed. To make it easier, lie closer together. To make it harder, stand two books up as a gate and blow the ball through it. A few breaths at a time, with rests in between. Five to ten minutes in all is plenty. Wash hands afterwards, because newspaper ink comes off on fingers. The game also works at bedtime, or on a stormy night.
activity.inClass: Pairs lie face to face on a mat, one paper ball per pair, with one adult for every four children. The adult leads one slow “whoooo” for everyone, and all the balls roll at once. Then the other child in each pair blows. Everyone washes hands afterwards.
